code: exif_data_load_data (ExifData *data, const unsigned char *d_orig, unsigned int ds)
note: Attacker-controlled EXIF buffer (raw EXIF: 'Exif\0\0' header + TIFF IFD0 containing a 9-byte MakerNote entry) enters the parser together with its length ds.

The MakerNote entry (tag 0x927c, format UNDEFINED, 9 components) gets a heap allocation of exactly s=9 bytes holding 'Apple iOS' without a NUL terminator; entry->size = 9, so the buffer is not NUL-terminated and has no slack.
After IFD0 is loaded, the MakerNote entry (9 bytes, 'Apple iOS') is fetched from the parsed data and passed to the maker-note identify dispatcher.
Olympus, Canon, Fuji and Pentax identify functions all return 0 for this MakerNote (their size/magic checks fail), so control reaches exif_mnote_data_apple_identify.

Root cause: the identify function compares e->data against the NUL-terminated literal "Apple iOS" with strcmp without first checking that e->size is large enough to contain the string plus terminator; with e->size == 9 (no NUL) the comparison runs past the allocation.

Sink: all 9 bytes match the prefix of "Apple iOS", so strcmp dereferences e->data[9] looking for the NUL terminator, which lies beyond the 9-byte heap buffer - out-of-bounds read (heap-buffer-overflow).
